summary: Unexpected long-tail latency during hourly batch inference; clients report apparent timeouts
description: Customer NimbleDocs reports recurring long-tail latency spikes (30s-90s) during their scheduled hourly batch inference jobs. From the customer perspective the SDK requests appear to hang or timeout intermittently; their app surface shows cascading retries and slower user-visible responses. They are on a dedicated plan in us-east and run batches with concurrency=40 and short per-request payloads (summary/simple-chunking).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Schedule a batch run of 10k short inference requests using NimbleDocs SDK v0.9.4 with concurrency=40.
2) Observe client-side measured RTs: many requests complete <250ms but a long-tailed subset show 30s+ wall time or client timeout.
3) Capture client logs showing repeated 429 responses followed by immediate retries without exponential backoff jitter.
4) Inspect gateway logs for the same time window to correlate request IDs and rate-limit headers.
observed_logs: 2026-03-10T14:01:02Z req=req_0a1b2c path=/v1/generate status=429 x-rate-limit-limit=1200 x-rate-limit-remaining=0 x-rate-limit-reset=25
Customer-provided stack trace: SDK v0.9.4 RetryManager: immediate-retry triggered after 429 (no jitter configured)
comments: Maya Rodriguez (Support): Received initial report from NimbleDocs — they see a small percent of requests taking 30-90s during their hourly batch. They included SDK logs and a short repro script.
NimbleDocs (Customer): 'This started ~2026-03-08 after we increased batch concurrency. UX impact is intermittent but affects our search indexing pipeline.'
Jonah Kim (SRE): Beginning correlation with API gateway and rate-limiter logs for 14:00-14:10 window on 2026-03-10.
SRE note: Found repeated 429s for same client token followed by rapid client retries. Gateway reported rate-limit-remaining=0 and reset window ~20-30s.
investigation_notes: Correlated request IDs between customer logs and gateway: confirmed series of 429 responses arriving before a successful 200 for many request IDs.

Gateway behavior: We enforce a per-customer sliding window soft quota for dedicated customers in addition to global rate limits. When remaining hits 0 we return 429 and set x-rate-limit-reset to the remaining seconds in the window.

Customer SDK behavior: NimbleDocs SDK v0.9.4 default RetryManager retries on 429 immediately with fixed short delays and no jitter by default. This caused many concurrent requests to retry into the same reset window (amplification).

Serving pool: transient backpressure — when many retries re-enter the system at the same time, serving pool saturates (observed pool-util > 90%), which increases queuing and wall-time for the few requests that are accepted leading to long-tail latencies.
We reproduced locally by running the customer's repro with the SDK configured to remove jitter: same long-tail pattern appears when concurrency >= 32 and per-customer quota windows are active.
We verified SDK v0.10.x includes configurable jitter/exponential backoff defaults that mitigate the spike (internal tests show 6x reduction in peak queue depth).
resolution_notes: - Recommended immediate change: set SDK retry policy to exponential backoff with jitter; recommended config: initial_delay=300ms, max_retries=5, jitter=0.4. Sent sample config snippet and a hotfix patch for their fork.
- Workaround: lower batch concurrency from 40 -> 12 for the scheduled hourly jobs until quota-increasing request completes.

- Applied a temporary increase to their soft quota window for 2 hours at 2026-03-10T16:00Z to let their queued jobs drain (operation performed by CapacityOps team; ticket INT-1209 records the quota bump).

- Engineering to update rate-limiter to emit clearer Retry-After behavior and ensure x-retry-after header is present for all 429s from soft quota (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8842).
- Add telemetry alert for per-customer retry storms that push serving-pool-util >85% (EPIC: INT-1345).
- Update public SDK defaults to enable jittered exponential backoff and document recommended settings in the 'Batching and Rate Limits' guide (Docs PR drafted).

Outcome: NimbleDocs confirmed their next hourly run on 2026-03-11 completed without long-tail spikes after applying SDK config and temporary quota bump. Marking customer-facing incident mitigated; follow-ups scheduled for platform fixes.
